page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.8-128 is a flexible compute instance powered by AMD EPYC 9J14 processors running on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 8 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading, providing 16 vCPUs operating at a nominal clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, yielding a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, or 8.0 GB of memory per core, which suits memory-bound workloads.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, meaning persistent data management requires external block volume attachments or network storage mounts. Networking provision includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the compute and memory resources can be scaled independently under the flexible E5 architecture, this profile maintains a dedicated allocation that eliminates resource contention across cores.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of dedicated Zen-based AMD compute cores and high memory density delivers consistent thread isolation. The high memory ratio makes VM.Standard.E5.Flex.8-128 well adapted for in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, enterprise resource planning services, search indexing, and large data processing pipelines where dataset residency in memory avoids storage serialization bottlenecks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.8-128 is a flexible virtual compute instance configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs based on the AMD EPYC 9J14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture with a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, the system is provisioned with 128.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio suitable for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. There are zero dedicated GPUs and no local NVMe storage drives included, requiring persistent workloads to utilize network-attached storage or managed block volumes. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance. Because of its dedicated core allocation and substantial memory capacity, the instance operates reliably for in-memory databases, memory-resident analytics, caching platforms, and data engineering pipelines.
